label: monk2-s2
summary: The model scores a case by how many of the six attributes sit at their first value: a1, a2, a4, a5 and a6 each lower the score through their own direct edges, and a3 lowers it through gate 435, which is on for the 168 training rows with a3=2 and off for the others (0 rows with a3=1 have it on, 0 with a3=2 have it off). Adding first values one at a time from the case with none takes the score from 86.2 to 2.6 at four and -19.8 at five. Over the full input space the model predicts positive for 100% of cells with three first values, 49% with four and 0% with five; the rule "at most three first values" agrees on 408 of 432 cells. The MONK-2 class needs exactly two, so the model has the upper cut but not the lower one: it predicts positive for 203 of the 232 negative training rows, giving a training accuracy of 41.2% at an AUC of 0.808. Units 1083 and 2445 are never on in training (0 and 0 rows on); unit 639 is a small a3 offset.
